issues.t: Air bag monitor can short out from water, causing smoke or fire (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light flashes or stays on, the horn blows by itself, warning lights flicker, or there is a burning smell, smoke or a fire from the dash. In rare cases the airbags went off with no crash.
issues.why: Water from a leaking heater core or other liquid can get into the airbag monitor under the dash and short it out. Recall 02V-323 adds a shield over the monitor and greases its connector. This is the most-reported problem on the 1997 Tracer.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning from the dash, pull over, turn the car off and get out. Check the recall with your VIN at NHTSA or a Ford dealer. Fix any heater core leak or damp carpet right away.

issues.t: Valve seat drops out and damages the engine
issues.sym: A ticking like a noisy lifter, then a misfire, check engine light, loss of power, or sudden engine failure at speed.
issues.why: On the 2.0L engine, a valve seat (the hard ring the valve closes against) can come loose from the aluminum cylinder head, often after the engine has run hot. The loose seat can wreck the valve, piston and head.
issues.next: If you hear new ticking or the engine misfires, stop driving hard and have the cylinder head checked. Once a seat drops, repairs usually mean a new head or a used engine, so get a quote before deciding.

issues.sym: A cracking or clunking from the rear, the car sitting low or leaning, a coil rubbing the body, or uneven rear tire wear. Some cars failed state inspection.
issues.why: The rear coil springs rust and snap near the strut, often around 50,000 to 60,000 miles. It is one of the most common complaints on these Tracers.
issues.next: Look at the rear springs for a broken coil. Replace springs in pairs and check the struts and tires at the same time. A broken spring can cut a tire, so don't put it off.
issues.sevReason: A broken coil spring usually leaves the car sagging; get checked soon (technician to confirm).

issues.sym: Hard or jerky shifts, slipping, a delay before Reverse engages, or the transmission quitting altogether.
issues.why: The automatic shared with the Ford Escort wears out internally. Owners of both cars report failures, some around 50,000 to 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it is slipping or slow to engage, avoid hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis. A used transmission is often a practical option instead of a rebuild on a car this old.

issues.t: Engine surges or speeds up while braking
issues.sym: The engine revs up or the car pushes forward while you are braking or stopped, or it speeds up after you lift off the gas.
issues.why: NHTSA reports don't name one cause. A sticking throttle, a faulty idle air control valve or a bad throttle position sensor can all raise the idle on these engines.
issues.next: If it surges, keep firm pressure on the brake, shift to Neutral and turn the engine off once safely stopped. Have a shop check the throttle, idle air control valve and sensors before driving again.

issues.sym: The horn blows on its own while driving or parked and keeps going until the fuse is pulled. Some owners also had airbag warnings.
issues.why: The horn circuit runs through the steering wheel near the airbag. On 1997 cars it's often tied to the airbag monitor short. A worn horn contact or damaged wiring can also cause it.
issues.next: Pull the horn fuse or relay to stop it, then have the horn switch and wiring checked. On a 1997, ask about the airbag monitor recall.

issues.sym: A sudden clunk or wobble at the front of the engine, a thrown belt, or loss of power steering and charging.
issues.why: The rubber layer in the crankshaft pulley can break down, letting the outer ring slip or come off. Owners reported it at about 40,000 miles and up, and in one case it damaged the timing belt.
issues.next: If you see the pulley wobble or the belt jump, stop and have it towed. Replace the pulley and check the drive belt and timing belt.

issues.sym: A strong fuel smell or gas dripping under the car, often near the rear.
issues.why: Owners reported cracked tanks and split tank seams. A related fuel-tank cracking recall covered some 1995 models in certain states.
issues.next: Don't drive or park in a closed garage with a fuel leak. Have it towed to a shop and replace the tank.

issues.sym: One or both headlights go out, flicker, or the plug behind the bulb looks brown or melted.
issues.why: The headlight connectors get too hot and melt. Owners on both sides of the car reported it.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the lights fail at night. Replace the melted plugs and check the headlight switch and wiring.

issues.sym: The headlight covers turn yellow or cloudy and the lights look dim at night.
issues.why: The plastic lenses break down in sunlight.
issues.next: Try a headlight restoration kit, or replace the lenses for the best light.

issues.t: Brake pedal goes soft or brakes fail
issues.sym: The pedal sinks, feels stiff or shudders, the brakes grind, or a rear wheel locks under light braking.
issues.why: Owners reported leaking caliper seals, a failed master cylinder, worn rotors and broken pad clips.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Don't drive if the pedal sinks. Check the fluid level and have the calipers, lines and master cylinder inspected.

issues.t: Ignition switch fails or key won't come out
issues.sym: The key won't come out of the ignition, the engine won't crank or stalls right after starting.
issues.why: Owners reported worn ignition switches and lock cylinders.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in Park. If the problem keeps coming back, have the ignition switch and lock cylinder replaced.

issues.t: Replacement seat belts may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. Only some replacement driver's belts are affected.
issues.why: Some TRW replacement driver's seat belts made in December 2002 for these cars don't lock in a crash. Recall 04E-048 covers the bad parts.
issues.next: If your driver's belt was ever replaced, check the recall with NHTSA and have the belt checked.

issues.t: Alternator fails or battery light comes on
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, the lights dim, or the car dies with a dead battery. One owner also lost power steering.
issues.why: Owners reported alternators failing, and in one case loose alternator nuts.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on while you're driving, turn off everything you don't need (A/C, radio, seat heaters) and drive only as far as a safe place off the road, not a long trip. If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering gets heavy, stop and turn the engine off. Your owner's manual may say what your car needs; follow it. Have the charging system tested. Replace the alternator if it's weak and check its mounting bolts and belt.

issues.t: Exhaust leak and fumes in the cabin
issues.sym: An exhaust smell inside the car, a louder exhaust or steam and ticking from the engine.
issues.why: Owners reported a cracked exhaust manifold, a broken exhaust pipe and an opening in the firewall that let fumes in.
issues.next: Drive with the windows down and get it checked quickly. Headaches or drowsiness while driving mean you should stop and get out. Have the manifold, pipes and firewall seals inspected.

issues.sym: The transmission stays in third gear and won't shift, often after the engine bay gets wet.
issues.why: The transmission range sensor tells the computer which gear is chosen. Water can short it out.
issues.next: Avoid spraying water in the engine bay. Have a shop scan for codes and replace the sensor if it's bad.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure, misfire or engine dies
issues.sym: The engine misfires, runs rough or dies, and only two spark plugs get spark.
issues.why: The engine uses a coil pack that fires two plugs per side. When one side of the coil fails, two cylinders stop firing.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the coil, plugs and wires tested. A failed coil pack is a fairly simple fix.

issues.sym: Coolant drips, a low coolant level, the temperature gauge climbing, or steam from the engine.
issues.why: Owners reported leaking core (freeze) plugs and radiators. Overheating is closely tied to valve seat failure on the 2.0L engine.
issues.next: Pull over if the gauge climbs. Find and fix any leak right away, since overheating can ruin the cylinder head.

issues.sym: A grinding or roaring noise from a front wheel that gets louder with speed.
issues.why: Front wheel bearings wear out. One owner replaced the front bearings and coil springs at about 104,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the wheel bearings checked. A failing bearing can overheat and let the wheel wobble.

issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and stays on, sometimes with no other symptom.
issues.why: Common causes include emission sensors, ignition parts and the fuel vapor system.
issues.next: Have the codes read for free at a parts store, then fix the cause.

issues.sym: The dash top comes unglued and curls, making the windshield harder to defrost.
issues.why: The dash covering separates from its base with heat and age.
issues.next: Have it glued or covered if it blocks the defroster vents.

issues.sym: The motorized shoulder belt stops partway or the driver's belt locks up.
issues.why: The motor or track that moves the automatic belt wears out.
issues.next: Wear the manual lap belt and have the belt motor and track repaired.

issues.t: Power steering pump noise or failure
issues.sym: A whine when turning, or the steering suddenly becomes heavy.
issues.why: Owners reported power steering pump failures.
issues.next: Check the fluid level. If it's low, look for leaks. A failing pump should be replaced before it quits.
issues.sevReason: Pump noise or wear; assist fades gradually.

issues.t: Hard starting from a sticking idle air valve
issues.sym: The engine cranks a long time before starting, then stalls.
issues.why: The idle air control valve can stick and fail to let enough air in for starting.
issues.next: Have the valve cleaned or replaced. It's usually a small job.

issues.t: No-start from oil in the distributor
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, and there's oil inside the distributor cap.
issues.why: A seal inside the distributor fails and lets engine oil in, which ruins the ignition parts.
issues.next: Have the distributor checked. Replacing the distributor or its seal usually fixes it.

issues.sym: A knocking sound when braking gently.
issues.why: Worn caliper slide sleeves let the caliper move and knock.
issues.next: Have the calipers checked and the slides replaced or lubricated.

issues.sym: A whine from the manual transmission when you lift off the gas.
issues.why: The teeth on the idler gear may have been machined incorrectly.
issues.next: Check the gear oil level. If the whine gets worse or the gears grind, have the transmission inspected.

issues.sym: The horn doesn't sound, or only works if you press very hard.
issues.why: A poor ground connection in the steering column.
issues.next: Have the horn ground and contacts cleaned or repaired.
